Thanks Aditya — received and skimmed. A couple quick clarifying questions before the call at 10:00 PT: 

1) The sample shows request_id and user_id_hash. Do you also retain a mapping table that allows re-identification for lawful requests (i.e., internal only, for customer debug/supported requests)? If so, what is the retention window for that mapping?
2) For auth_result, do you log the auth mechanism (SAML/OIDC/ApiKey) or just the outcome?
3) For retention policy: can you confirm the default logs retention for access logs vs. aggregated metrics? We saw a note about 90 days in the CAIQ draft but want to confirm S3 lifecycle rules.

If you can answer those quickly, we'll decide whether to take the call or push to a 30-minute follow-up next week.

-Dana

On Wed, Jan 21, 2026 at 10:12 AM Dana Liu <dana.liu@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Thanks Aditya — received and skimmed. A couple quick clarifying questions before the call at 10:00 PT:
>
> 1) The sample shows request_id and user_id_hash. Do you also retain a mapping table that allows re-identification for lawful requests (i.e., internal only, for customer debug/supported requests)? If so, what is the retention window for that mapping?
> 2) For auth_result, do you log the auth mechanism (SAML/OIDC/ApiKey) or just the outcome?
> 3) For retention policy: can you confirm the default logs retention for access logs vs. aggregated metrics? We saw a note about 90 days in the CAIQ draft but want to confirm S3 lifecycle rules.

Hi Dana — quick answers inline below so you have them for the call: 

1) Re-identification mapping: we do not keep a reversible mapping as part of daily access logs we hand off. For debugging we can generate a scoped trace that correlates hashed user_id to internal ids, but that trace is ephemeral and only accessible to authorized SRE for 30 days. We can provide SOC2 controls describing approval workflow.

2) Auth mechanism: the sample contains an auth_type field (SAML/OIDC/API_KEY), we accidentally omitted from the first extract; we will include it in the next sample after the call if you prefer. The high-level log shows auth_result but auth_type is logged at debug level and available on request.

3) Retention: access logs are kept in hot storage for 90 days by default; aggregated metrics (counts, latencies) are retained 13 months. S3 lifecycle moves raw logs to Glacier after 90 days by default for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention with their contract.

Action items before call (Marissa/Aditya):
- Aditya: prepare a one-slide summary of re-identification workflow and approval gates.
- Marissa: add auth_type column to the sample file and resend if Dana wants it.
- Soojin: pull SOC2 control reference snippets for the re-identification approval process.

If you'd prefer to reschedule the 10:00 PT call to 11:00 PT to give us 30 min to update the files, we can do that.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
